games.title: Pong
games.note: Allan Alcorn built it as a training exercise; the first Pong cabinet was tested in a California bar.

games.title: Maze War
games.note: Players moved through a maze in first person and shot each other, years before Doom.

games.title: Speed Race
games.note: Designed by Tomohiro Nishikado, later the creator of Space Invaders.

games.title: Gun Fight
games.note: Midway's US version was among the first arcade games to use a microprocessor.

games.title: Colossal Cave Adventure
games.note: The first text adventure, based on a real cave system in Kentucky.

games.title: Breakout
games.note: Steve Wozniak worked on the prototype for Atari.

games.title: Combat
games.note: Came packed in with the Atari 2600 at launch.

games.title: Gee Bee
games.note: Namco's first video game.

games.title: Space Invaders
games.note: Tomohiro Nishikado designed and programmed it.

games.title: Adventure
games.note: Warren Robinett hid his name in a secret room, the first well-known Easter egg.

games.title: Ball (Game & Watch)
games.note: The first Game & Watch, designed by Gunpei Yokoi.

games.title: Rogue
games.note: Gave its name to the roguelike genre.

games.title: Space Panic
games.note: Often named as an ancestor of the platform game.

games.title: Radar Scope
games.note: Its poor sales in the US led Nintendo to convert the cabinets to Donkey Kong.

games.title: Mystery House
games.note: Roberta and Ken Williams made it; it was one of the first graphic adventures.

games.title: Zork II: The Wizard of Frobozz
Wizardry: Proving Grounds of the Mad Overlord
Ultima II: The Revenge of the Enchantress
Star Wars: The Empire Strikes Back
Advanced Dungeons and Dragons: Treasure of Tarmin
Football Manager
games.note: Kevin Toms wrote it; it is often called the first football management game.

games.title: Zaxxon
games.note: The first arcade game to use isometric graphics.

games.title: River Raid
games.note: Designed by Carol Shaw.

games.title: E.T. the Extra-Terrestrial
games.note: Howard Scott Warshaw built it in about five weeks.

games.title: Ant Attack
games.note: Sandy White; one of the first games with a free-moving isometric 3D view.

games.title: Chuckie Egg
games.note: Nigel Alderton wrote it at age 19.

games.title: Bomberman
games.note: Hudson's first Bomberman, years before the Famicom version.

games.title: I, Robot
games.note: Considered the first commercial 3D polygon-filled arcade game.

games.title: One on One: Dr. J vs. Larry Bird
The Seven Cities of Gold
games.note: Designed by Dan Bunten at Ozark Softscape.

games.title: Raid on Bungeling Bay
games.note: Will Wright's map editor for this game grew into SimCity.

games.title: The Hitchhiker's Guide to the Galaxy
games.note: Written with Douglas Adams, who also contributed the plot.

games.title: The Lords of Midnight
games.note: Mike Singleton designed this war game with a huge, 4,000-location landscape.

games.title: Karate Champ
games.note: Often credited as the game that set up the one-on-one fighting game.

games.title: Match Day
games.note: Jon Ritman programmed it; it was a long-running Spectrum football series.

games.title: King's Quest II: Romancing the Throne
Chaos: The Battle of Wizards
games.note: Julian Gollop wrote this wizard duel; it was an early step toward his later strategy games.

games.title: Spy vs. Spy II: The Island Caper
Ultima IV: Quest of the Avatar
games.note: Richard Garriott's game where the goal is to become a good person, not to kill a villain.

games.title: Monty on the Run
games.note: The C64 music by Rob Hubbard is a famous soundtrack.
